entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Antonius Rufinus (b. 50 CE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in the Roman Empire. Known for his military leadership and command roles, he played a significant role in the governance of the Eastern Roman Empire during the reign of Emperor Marcus Aurelius. Rufinus' legacy extends to the historical records of the Roman Empire, providing valuable insights into the administrative and military structures of the time.


Rufinus' tenure as a civil administrator spanned over two decades, during which he was responsible for various administrative and military duties. He was instrumental in the Roman Empire's efforts to expand its borders and maintain its territorial integrity. Rufinus' contributions to the Roman Empire's governance and military strategy are still studied by historians today.


The Roman Empire's expansion and territorial consolidation during Rufinus' tenure had a lasting impact on the region, shaping the course of Western civilization. His legacy can be seen in the development of the Eastern Roman Empire, which would eventually become a major power in its own right.


Rufinus' contributions to the historical record of the Roman Empire have been widely recognized. His writings and administrative records provide a unique window into the inner workings of the Roman Empire's government and military.
